page.title: How to Choose a Webinar Production Company
page.description: Compare production partners on scope, staffing, tools and cost models so you can pick the right crew for your next webinar or summit.
page.h1: How do you choose the right webinar production partner?
page.definition: A webinar production company is a service provider that plans, rehearses and runs live virtual events on your chosen platform, delivering a run of show, speaker prep, branded assets, live moderation, backup streaming and edited recordings.
page.quick_answer: Match the production scope to your event type: a single producer for a simple webinar, a full crew for a summit. Verify they work on your platform, own the run of show and deliver a replay within 48 hours.

sections.h2: What services should a webinar production company include?

blocks.p: A complete production package covers every live‑event workstream so your team only handles content and promotion.

ul: Run of show with timed cues and owner per segment
Speaker brief, tech check and full rehearsal on the real platform
Branded slide template, lower thirds and transition graphics
Live producer calling cues and a platform operator managing scenes
Q&A moderation and chat triage during the session
Backup stream on a second encoder or platform
Edited recording and short clips delivered within 48 hours

sections.h2: How do staffing needs change with event size?

blocks.p: Headcount scales with complexity; a single producer can run a straightforward webinar while summits and hybrid events need specialised roles.

head: Event type
Typical crew
rows: One producer handling cues, platform and moderation
Show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator
All summit roles plus venue AV liaison and stream engineer

sections.h2: Which platforms do production companies support?

blocks.p: Production is platform‑agnostic; the crew works inside the software you already licence.

ul: Zoom Webinars and Zoom Events
Microsoft Teams Live Events
ON24 and Cvent
StreamYard, Livestorm and Goldcast
Bizzabo and Hopin

sections.h2: What are the common cost models and price ranges?

blocks.p: Production fees are separate from platform licences and follow three main models.

ul: Moderated webinars: $2,500 to $7,500 per production
Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions: $10,000 to $50,000 and above
Custom scopes quoted per engagement; no fixed price list published

sections.h2: What timeline should you plan for?

blocks.p: Lead time depends on event scale and whether the format is new or repeatable.

ol: Webinar: three to four weeks from brief to live
Summit or online conference: six to eight weeks
Hybrid conference: six to eight weeks with venue AV locked before agenda final
One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live
Technical check 60 minutes before stream start

sections.h2: How do you evaluate a production partner before signing?

blocks.p: Use a short checklist to compare vendors on the factors that affect delivery quality.

ul: Proven experience on your chosen platform
Named producer who owns the run of show end‑to‑end
Backup stream plan documented in the proposal
Replay and clip turnaround committed to 48 hours
Clear scope that separates platform fees from production fees
References from events of similar size and format

faq.q: Do I need a production company if I already have a webinar platform licence?
faq.a: Yes. The platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. Someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

faq.q: Can a production company help me choose the right platform?
faq.a: West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it based on your format, audience size and integration needs.

faq.q: What deliverables should I expect after the live event?
faq.a: Edited recording, short clips for social, attendee engagement report and a post‑event debrief document. Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a production team for a summit?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. A summit needs six to eight weeks of management; a webinar three to four.

faq.q: Does the production company handle registration and follow‑up emails?
faq.a: Typical tools: Zoom Events, Cvent or Bizzabo for the event; Eventbrite or Cvent for registration; Asana or Monday.com for the plan; HubSpot or Salesforce for follow‑up. Production crews focus on live delivery; marketing ops owns registration and nurture.
